Hi Markus / Laura —

Thanks for the quick follow-up. Our three execs are available next week but only during narrow windows:
- US (James): typically 08:00–11:00 PST local
- EU (Elena): 14:00–17:00 CET local
- APAC (Li Wei): 09:00–12:00 SGT local

Because the meeting needs to include all three decision-makers, we tried to find overlap and came up with two candidate blocks:
A) 15:00 UTC — maps to 07:00 PST / 16:00 CET / 23:00 SGT (early for US, late for APAC)
B) 20:00 UTC — maps to 12:00 PST / 21:00 CET / 04:00 SGT (works for US/EU but kills APAC)

We realize DST labeling has been flaky on our side (some invites show CEST instead of CET); if possible let's use UTC anchors to avoid the +1/−1 confusion.

Quick ask: can you confirm which of A/B works, or propose a two-part approach (short global sync + regional follow-ups)?

Thanks —
Elena

- Option 2: 17:00 UTC (09:00 PST / 18:00 CET / 01:00 SGT) — better for US morning, worse for APAC

If Cerulean can do a 60-min global kickoff at one of those anchors and we offer a 30–45 minute regional deep-dive for APAC the next day (recorded deep dive for those who can't attend live), that might be the cleanest path.

Hi all — quick note from ops:

We're seeing Cerulean calendar invites show "CEST " in the event metadata even though the event is in December (post-DST). That is what's causing a persistent 1-hour mapping error for some folks in EU. To avoid more back-and-forth, can we pick times using UTC in both the invite title and the calendar body?

Concrete proposal (UTC anchors + local mapping):
- Tue 2026-12-15 15:00 UTC — 07:00 PST / 16:00 CET / 23:00 SGT (good for US exec if early start ok)
- Tue 2026-12-15 18:00 UTC — 10:00 PST / 19:00 CET / 02:00 SGT (suits EU and US later morning)
- Wed 2026-12-16 01:00 UTC — 17:00 PST / 18:00 CET / 09:00 SGT (APAC morning friendly)

If Cerulean confirms which anchor they prefer, we'll send a single UTC-labeled invite and include local mappings in the event description to avoid CEST/CET auto-labeling.

—Laura

Thanks — I checked with the execs. Summary:
- James (US) can do early mornings but not before 06:30 PST; 07:00–09:00 PST is workable.
- I (EU) am flexible in late afternoon (16:00–18:00 CET).
- Li Wei (APAC) strongly prefers 09:00–11:00 SGT (their local morning).

Given those constraints, Option 3 from Markus (01:00 UTC = 09:00 SGT on Wed) gets Li Wei best attendance but forces James to be late evening (17:00 PST previous day) which he doesn't prefer.

Li Wei suggested a two-part plan: a 30-minute global alignment that focuses on decision criteria (UTC anchor — short, recorded), and a separately scheduled APAC deep-dive at 09:00 SGT next day. That preserves live APAC participation and lets James and our EU exec dial into a shorter decision meeting at a tolerable hour.

We like the two-part approach if Redwood can accommodate.

—Elena
Elena Rossi | Head of Integrations | Cerulean AI
